# [Perf] paged-experts: exact size pinning

## Motivation

This PR aims to decrease memory footprint.

Currently, the Paged Experts Feature (#42557) keeps every expert of the model in page-locked host memory. torch's pinned allocator rounds each allocation up to a power of two, so **a 402 MB `w13` tensor pins 512 MiB**. Across a model this pins about a third more than the experts need on Qwen3-30B-A3B, and 85% more on gpt-oss-20b. Pinned memory cannot be swapped, and it is often what decides whether a model fits: WSL2, for example, caps it at about half of RAM.

## Modifications

`store.py`:
- The pinned host store allocates through HiCache's host allocator (`alloc_with_host_register` with `HostTensorAllocator`). That maps exactly the tensor's size (huge pages with `SGLANG_HUGEPAGE_SIZE`), pre-faults it and registers it with CUDA.
- The gather kernel reads it through `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` as before.
- A store only staged for a repack stays pageable, as before.

## Accuracy Tests

The experts' bytes are unchanged; only their allocation differs.

**Kernel test.** The store pins exactly its size, and the gather kernel reads it.

**Paged vs unpaged, 4-layer test models** (E=32, top-4, K=8; prompt and greedy decode logprobs; RTX 5070 Ti; main 2d3de82633 and this PR in one run):

| model | runner | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-MoE bf16 | triton | identical | identical |
| AWQ int4 | Marlin | decode max 0.014 | decode max 0.014 |
| compressed-tensors NVFP4 | Marlin | median max 0.078, unpaged floor 0.059 | median max 0.059, unpaged floor 0.063 |

Marlin is not run-to-run reproducible, so the Marlin formats are judged against the spread of two unpaged servers (the floor); bf16 on triton is bit-identical. Each check has a negative control that must fail (a perturbed RMSNorm eps on bf16 and AWQ, unnormalized top-k weights on NVFP4), and all three do.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same machine as #42557: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (PCIe 5.0 x16, 62 GB RAM), Qwen3-30B-A3B, 10,240 KV tokens and 4 slots, prefix caching off, 16 ShareGPT warm-up requests discarded. Decode tok/s is `1000 / median TPOT` over 8 ShareGPT prompts sent one at a time (256 output tokens each); TTFT and ITL are from the same requests. 4 requests: 16 ShareGPT prompts from 4 clients at once (output tok/s). 2k TTFT: 4 natural ~2,048-token prompts. main (upstream 2d3de82633) is measured first and last in the same run as this PR; both values are shown, and a difference inside their spread is no difference. Pinned host memory is `Shmem` in `/proc/meminfo` once serving (the new allocator maps the store shared; torch's pinned allocator counted there too).

| config | pinned host memory | weight load | decode tok/s | TTFT p50 / p99 | 4 requests: out tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| int4, K=92: main | 18.6 GiB | 37.1 / 45.2 s | 211.8 / 212.8 | 51 / 88, 50 / 82 ms | 400 / 401 |
| int4, K=92: this PR | **13.9 GiB** (−25%) | 37.7 s | 212.0 | 50 / 87 ms | 398 |
| FP8, K=40: main | 36.0 GiB | 48.7 / 48.3 s | 90.3 / 90.3 | 213 / 301, 218 / 301 ms | 100 / 99 |
| FP8, K=40: this PR | **27.0 GiB** (−25%) | 54.7 s | 90.3 | 213 / 301 ms | 100 |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: main | 20.3 GiB | 45.2 / 44.9 s | 189.8 / 192.9 | 72 / 119, 73 / 116 ms | 352 / 349 |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: this PR | **15.2 GiB** (−25%) | 45.4 s | 190.3 | 72 / 121 ms | 351 |

Decode, TTFT and throughput are unchanged; the store pins a quarter less on all three formats (power-of-two rounding cost a third more than the experts need). Pre-faulting the exact-size mapping adds about 6 s to FP8's weight load (27 GiB of store); the 45.2 s is one slow boot of main.


## CI

The kernel test checks that the store pins exactly its size and that the gather reads it.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@N3mezis Could you add the matching cleanup for the new host allocation? `alloc_with_host_register()` calls `cudaHostRegister`, but the returned mmap-backed tensor only unmaps its storage when freed; it does not call `cudaHostUnregister`. HiCache pairs this allocator with explicit unregister calls in `HostKVCache.destroy()`, while `HostExpertStore` has no equivalent cleanup.

Please pair registration with unregister before releasing the mapping, after outstanding GPU reads have finished. Tie cleanup to the actual buffer lifetime: the new test retains `host` after its temporary `HostExpertStore` is gone, so a store destructor alone would be too early. One focused allocation/release regression test should be enough.

Tie cleanup to the actual buffer lifetime: the new test retains `host` after its temporary `HostExpertStore` is gone, so a store destructor alone would be too early. Thanks, good catch! Fixed in a32258a322, and the allocation is simpler for it:

- Each pinned store tensor is now shared memory of exactly its size (`memfd` + `torch.UntypedStorage.from_file`), registered with CUDA in place, as multimodal_gen's layerwise offload pins its stores. It no longer goes through HiCache's allocator: that allocator pairs with an explicit `destroy()`, and the tensor it returns releases its mapping itself, with no point to unregister before that. Tying the unregister to the buffer's lifetime on top of it took a second tensor over the same pages, only to have an object whose death we could hook. With memory we allocate and register ourselves, the finalizer sits on the one storage that owns the pages, so the registration and the memory share a single lifetime.
- A `weakref.finalize` on the storage ties the registration to the buffer's lifetime: it runs when the last tensor or view on the storage is freed, synchronizes the device so queued page-in copies and gather reads have finished, and unregisters the pages while they are still mapped; then torch releases them. A failed unregister is logged.
- New kernel test `test_store_unregisters_its_pages_once_the_last_tensor_is_freed`: a slice that outlives its `HostExpertStore` keeps the pages registered (with a non-blocking copy still queued); once it is freed, `cudaHostUnregister` on the address fails because nothing is registered there anymore.

@@ -2,10 +2,53 @@
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import logging
+import math
+import os
+import weakref
 from typing import Dict, Sequence, Tuple
 
 import torch
 
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def _pin_until_freed(shape, dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Page-locked host memory of exactly the tensor's size (torch's pinned allocator rounds
+    every allocation up to a power of two): shared memory of that size, registered with CUDA
+    in place, as multimodal_gen's layerwise offload does.
+
+    The registration lasts as long as the storage, so as long as any tensor or view on it.
+    When the storage is freed, the device first finishes its queued reads (page-in copies,
+    gather), then the pages are unregistered, before torch releases them. Stores live as long
+    as their model, so that sync happens only at exit or in tests.
+    """
+    nbytes = math.prod(shape) * dtype.itemsize
+    fd = os.memfd_create("sglang-paged-experts", os.MFD_CLOEXEC)
+    try:
+        os.ftruncate(fd, nbytes)
+        storage = torch.UntypedStorage.from_file(
+            f"/proc/self/fd/{fd}", shared=True, nbytes=nbytes
+        )
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+    rc = int(torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostRegister(storage.data_ptr(), nbytes, 0))
+    if rc != 0:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Paged experts: cudaHostRegister of {nbytes} bytes failed (error {rc})"
+        )
+    weakref.finalize(storage, _unregister, storage.data_ptr())
+    # On the CPU, as its storage, also under a default CUDA device (model construction).
+    return torch.empty(0, dtype=dtype, device="cpu").set_(storage, 0, tuple(shape))
+
+
+def _unregister(data_ptr: int) -> None:
+    if torch.cuda.is_initialized():
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    rc = int(torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostUnregister(data_ptr))
+    if rc != 0:
+        logger.warning("Paged experts: cudaHostUnregister failed (error %d)", rc)
+
 
 class HostExpertStore:
     """Holds all E experts of each paged tensor on the host, in the layer's GPU layout.
@@ -27,7 +70,9 @@ def __init__(self, layer, names: Sequence[str], num_experts: int, pin: bool = Tr
         }
 
     def _alloc(self, shape, dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
-        return torch.empty(shape, dtype=dtype, device="cpu", pin_memory=self.pin)
+        if not self.pin or math.prod(shape) == 0:
+            return torch.empty(shape, dtype=dtype, device="cpu")
+        return _pin_until_freed(shape, dtype)
 
     def page_in(self, layer, loads: Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]) -> None:
         """Copy each ``(expert, slot)`` pair's expert, of every paged tensor, into its slot."""

@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
+import threading
 import unittest
 
 import torch
@@ -123,6 +124,70 @@ def test_gather_copies_the_plan_for_every_tensor(self):
                 self.assertTrue(torch.equal(gpu[s].cpu(), host[e]))
             self.assertFalse(gpu[1].any())  # untouched
 
+    def test_store_pins_its_exact_size_and_the_gather_reads_it(self):
+        """The host store pins exactly its size (torch's pinned allocator rounds up to a power
+        of two), and the gather kernel reads it through the GPU."""
+        from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.paged_experts.store import HostExpertStore
+
+        gpu = torch.zeros(K, 3, 1000, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        host = HostExpertStore(SimpleNamespace(w=gpu), ["w"], num_experts=E).host["w"]
+        host.copy_(torch.randn(E, 3, 1000, dtype=torch.bfloat16))
+        self.assertTrue(host.is_pinned())
+        self.assertEqual(host.untyped_storage().nbytes(), E * 3 * 1000 * 2)
+        src = torch.tensor([5, 63] + [0] * (K - 2), dtype=torch.int32).cuda()
+        dst = torch.tensor([2, 0] + [0] * (K - 2), dtype=torch.int32).cuda()
+        count = torch.tensor([2], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+        paged_experts_gather(*_gather_args([host], [gpu]), src, dst, count)
+
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(gpu[2].cpu(), host[5]))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(gpu[0].cpu(), host[63]))
+
+    def test_store_is_on_the_host_under_a_default_cuda_device(self):
+        """Models are constructed under ``torch.device("cuda")``; a store created there (by
+        a format that pages its loaded rows as they are) is still pinned host memory."""
+        from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.paged_experts.store import HostExpertStore
+
+        gpu = torch.zeros(K, 3, 1000, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        with torch.device("cuda"):
+            host = HostExpertStore(SimpleNamespace(w=gpu), ["w"], num_experts=E).host[
+                "w"
+            ]
+        self.assertEqual(host.device.type, "cpu")
+        self.assertTrue(host.is_pinned())
+
+    def test_store_unregisters_its_pages_once_the_last_tensor_is_freed(self):
+        """The pinned pages stay registered while any tensor on them lives (here a slice that
+        outlives the store and its tensor), and are unregistered once the last one is freed."""
+        import gc
+        from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.paged_experts.store import HostExpertStore
+
+        gpu = torch.zeros(K, 3, 1000, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        store = HostExpertStore(SimpleNamespace(w=gpu), ["w"], num_experts=E)
+        ptr = store.host["w"].data_ptr()
+        expert = store.host["w"][5]
+        gpu[0].copy_(expert, non_blocking=True)  # a read still queued when it is freed
+        del store
+        gc.collect()
+        self.assertTrue(expert.is_pinned())
+
+        del expert
+        gc.collect()
+        # Unregistering again must fail: the pages are no longer registered. In a thread of its
+        # own, as CUDA keeps the error as the thread's last error for a later call to report.
+        rc = []
+        unregister = lambda: rc.append(int(torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostUnregister(ptr)))
+        thread = threading.Thread(target=unregister)
+        thread.start()
+        thread.join()
+        self.assertNotEqual(rc[0], 0)
+
     def test_graph_replays_decide_on_new_routing(self):
         """A captured decide + gather plans and pages each replay's routing, not the routing
         seen at capture."""
